newsitem.title: UK: London stocks head lower, Nikkei posts gains.
newsitem.headline: London stocks head lower, Nikkei posts gains.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - Stocks closed sharply lower, tracking Wall Street as the Dow weakened ahead of a widely expected rise in U.S. interest rates on Tuesday. Retreating from Friday's record close, the FTSE 100 index closed 48.7 points lower at 4,645.2, with decliners in a more than four-to-one majority.
FRANKFURT - The German stock market was closed for the Pentecost holiday. Regular trading will resume on Tuesday. On Friday the 30-share DAX index closed up 42.44 points at 3,604.55.
PARIS - The French share market was closed for a market holiday. On Friday the blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 8.27 points to 2,784.28.
ZURICH - Swiss shares were closed for a market holiday. On Friday the All-share Swiss Performance Index was up 9.99 points to 3,255.91.

TOKYO - Stocks finished at a high for the calendar year, as blue chips recovered after early losses brought on by a strong yen. The mood was cautious ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting on Tuesday. The 225-share Nikkei average added 165.02 points to 20,489.75.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed firmer, boosted chiefly by a rebound in property developers and despite the sharp weakness seen on Wall Street last week. The Hang Seng Index closed 46.45 points higher at 14,108.82.
SYDNEY - Stocks ended lower with a downbeat bank sector overpowering a bullish batch of mining shares. The All Ordinaries index lost 7.1 points to 2,531.0.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ended firmly down with the golds board falling sharply as the ailing bullion price suffered a renewed bout of weakness. The golds index lost 2.89 percent, or 35.5 points, to 1,192.8.

The wider market also suffered a weak day as the hangover from Friday's sharp fall on Wall Street made it itself felt in most of the main industrial stocks. The all-share index dropped 26.2 points to 7,116.6, as the industrials index fell 22.7 points to 8,398.5.
